headline: Canada: cannabis farm receipts jump 31.9% to C$855M in Q3 2026
dek: Statistics Canada data released on 24 November show licensed producers took in C$855 million in July to September, and C$2.26 billion in nine months.
key_points: Statistics Canada's farm cash receipts release on 24 November puts cannabis at C$855 million for July to September 2026, up 31.9% from C$648 million a year earlier.
For January to September, cannabis receipts reached C$2.255 billion, up 16.7% from C$1.933 billion.
Cannabis grew faster than Canadian crops overall, which rose 27.3% in the quarter, and out-earned corn, barley, soybeans and fresh potatoes.
Receipts are gross revenue to licensed producers, not profit or retail sales, and the 2026 figures are preliminary.
body: Canada's licensed cannabis growers had their strongest quarter on Statistics Canada's books in at least two years. Farm cash receipts for cannabis were C$855 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 31.9% from C$648 million in the same three months of 2025, according to the agency's selected-commodities table published on 24 November alongside its release on farm cash receipts for January to September.

Across the first nine months of the year, cannabis brought in C$2.255 billion, a gain of 16.7% on the C$1.933 billion recorded a year earlier. The Marijuana Herald first highlighted the cannabis lines, which do not appear in the release text itself and sit only in the data table.
## What the numbers measure

Farm cash receipts are gross revenue, not earnings. Statistics Canada says the series records money when farmers are paid, based mainly on monthly marketings and prices, and that the figures do not show farmers' bottom line. Costs, write-downs and debt service are outside the measure entirely.

Cannabis has been counted as a crop in this series since legalization. When the agency first published annual figures in May 2019, it described the line as the revenue of licensed cannabis producers: C$564.1 million in 2018, up from C$189.0 million in 2017, a jump it tied to the start of recreational sales in October 2018. In November 2024 it adjusted its estimation method for cannabis to better reflect the industry and revised the data back to 2020, with most of the change in New Brunswick. The agency has not published a provincial breakdown of cannabis receipts in this release.
The 2025 numbers are revised and the 2026 numbers are preliminary, so the quarter can move when full-year data arrive.
## How cannabis stacks up against other crops

The third-quarter growth outpaced Canadian agriculture as a whole. Total farm cash receipts rose 14.3% in the quarter to C$27.85 billion, and total crop receipts rose 27.3% to C$15.2 billion. On our arithmetic, cannabis made up about 5.6% of all crop receipts in the quarter and about 3.1% of all farm receipts.

In dollar terms, cannabis earned more in July to September than several familiar field crops did. Statistics Canada's table shows third-quarter receipts of C$527 million for corn, C$449 million for fresh potatoes, C$440 million for barley and C$418 million for soybeans. Barley and soybeans together came to C$858 million, almost exactly the cannabis figure. Cannabis also beat greenhouse vegetables at C$653 million, though it trailed floriculture and nursery at C$872 million.

It is still a long way behind the big two. Canola brought in C$4.52 billion in the quarter and wheat excluding durum C$3.18 billion. Canola was the main reason crop receipts rose so sharply this year: the release says canola receipts for the nine months rose C$3.4 billion, or 38.2%, on higher marketings, higher prices and a 23.0% rise in crushing.
> Cannabis is now a mid-sized Canadian crop by revenue: bigger than barley or soybeans in a quarter, but a fraction of canola.
## Where the extra money came from

Statistics Canada does not explain movements in the cannabis line, so the cause of the jump is not in the data. The quarter added about C$207 million over the same period of 2025, on our arithmetic, compared with about C$322 million added over the full nine months. That means the third quarter alone delivered nearly two-thirds of the year's growth.

Other federal data show demand and supply moving in the right direction for producers. Health Canada's market data page, last updated on 21 October, shows total cannabis sales of about 14.34 million units in June 2026, up 4% from a year earlier, while packaged inventory fell 3% to about 45.86 million units. Selling more while holding less stock is the pattern a recovering supply chain would show, though Health Canada counts units, not dollars.

Retail sales have also been growing. Statistics Canada data reported by New Cannabis Ventures put March 2026 retail cannabis sales at C$471.4 million, up 6.2% from a year earlier, with 2026 sales up 7.7% year to date at that point. Full-year retail sales were C$5.62 billion in 2025, up 4.1%. Receipts rising faster than retail sales suggests producers are capturing more of each sale or shipping more product to processors and exporters, but the data released this week cannot say which.
## The wider industry picture

Statistics Canada's April 2026 profile of the sector put cannabis sales at C$5.5 billion in fiscal 2024/25, up 6.1%, and government cannabis revenue at C$2.5 billion. It counted 377 indoor growers, 52 outdoor growers, 123 product manufacturers and 16 wholesalers in 2025, and 3,295 retail businesses with employees at the end of that year. Health Canada lists about 1.39 million square metres of indoor growing area and 680 hectares outdoors.

For listed Canadian producers, the receipts series is an industry-wide signal rather than a company result. As we reported on 23 November, SNDL renewed its share buyback after retiring 24.5 million shares, and producers including Aurora Cannabis and Organigram have reported their own quarters this autumn. The Statistics Canada figure covers all licensed producers, large and small.
## What to watch

Statistics Canada will publish full-year 2026 farm cash receipts on 26 February 2027, which will show whether the third-quarter pace held through the autumn harvest and the holiday quarter. Preliminary 2026 net farm income follows on 26 May 2027. Health Canada's next monthly market data update will show whether unit sales kept rising and inventory kept falling after June.
